category_title: At-risk four-year-olds from low-income families with context-dependent oral language proficiency
minimal_context: The student is playing in the block center during non-teaching directed time to develop communication skills with peers and adults.
dialogue:
TUTOR: What are you doing with those blocks?

STUDENT: I am going to build a castle in the block center.

TUTOR: Give some of those blocks to your friend.

STUDENT: (To peer) If you don’t give me that toy, you’ll be sorry!

TUTOR: Listen to me and follow directions.

STUDENT: No.

options.A: Use a First-Then statement or combine it with a visual schedule, such as 'First give your friend two blocks, then continue building the castle.'
options.B: Use open-ended questions, expansions, and recasts (repeating the student’s incorrect usage correctly) to engage the student during the block center activity.
options.C: Provide visual expectations or rules for the block center and display a visual chart with the time remaining for the current activity.
options.D: Before the student continues building, ask them to complete the sentence, 'When I play in the block center, behaviors I am going to leave behind are...'
